summary: Anil Vidyalankar works in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, where he earned a PhD. In 1988, he founded Sandhaan, where he served as director around 1999.

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud 2009). He held a post at the University of Delhi in 2012.

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1975–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993) as Professor in the Departments of Religion and Anthropology.

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where around 2002 she was professor of Chinese language and culture and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields. She studied at Columbia University (~1972–1982) and later held academic posts at the University of Michigan (1989–2003) and The New School (2004).

Anna Aurelia Esposito specializes in Indology. She earned an MA at the University of Tübingen in 1998, studied Indology and Cultural Anthropology at Heidelberg University, and served as Assistant Professor of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

Anna Balikci Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Supervised by Lionel Caplan, she earned a PhD from SOAS University of London, and also studied under Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of IsMEO in 1984, she later served as director of the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Federico II.
Anna M. Shields is a scholar in Sinology. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and at Princeton University (~2015).

Anna Madelyn Hennessey works in religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell.

Anna Sawerthal specializes in Tibetology. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and a PhD at Heidelberg University under Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer. She also studied with Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.
Anna Seidel was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Between approximately 1961 and 1968, she studied under teachers Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1972–1976). She later held faculty positions at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, where her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, with instruction from Klas Hagren and Barbro Eriksson.

Anne Carolyn Klein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, UW–Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and Tibetan lamas, she held posts at Harvard (~1987–1990), Rice (~1991), and Dawn Mountain, which she founded.

Anne Casile works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2010) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2013).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Harvard University (~1989–1997) under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart, later holding posts at the University of Virginia (~1997–2001) and Harvard University (2002).

Anne Feldhaus is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976), and held an academic post at Arizona State University (~1981).
